requirements_summary:
Workload: customer support assistant + knowledge base search (chat + embeddings + reranking). Traffic profile: predictable weekday ramp (08:30–10:00 local), plus occasional bursty incidents.

Key requirement: predictive scaling to pre-warm capacity before ramp, but must remain deterministic and never exceed a hard max bound (budget ceiling). Also wants a clear minimum baseline to protect p95 latency during ramp.

Performance targets (stated): p95 end-to-end latency < 900ms during ramp; avoid queue depth growth > 60s; time-to-recover from ramp spike < 5 minutes.

Deployment/security: VPC deployment required; SSO/SAML; audit logging for scaling policy changes + autoscaler decisions (who/when/why); retention controls (12+ months preferred) and SIEM export path; KMS integration; asking about EU data residency for one business unit.
notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise customer running a support platform with heavy weekday seasonality.
- Primary pain: daily ramp causes queue buildup + p95 latency regressions if scaling is purely reactive; previous vendor either over-provisioned all day or had cold starts.
- Secondary pain: finance requires a strict cost ceiling. Quote from discovery: “We need a hard max. If the system decides to scale, it can’t surprise us.”

Current state / evaluation status
- Evaluating Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) + autoscaling policy controls.
- Pilot scope: 1 Dedicated deployment in us-east-1, targeting support-agent traffic + reranker.
- They are responsive and technical; security + procurement involved early.

Traffic profile (from calls)
- Weekday ramp: roughly 2–3x within ~60–90 minutes in the morning; stable midday; smaller ramp again late afternoon.
- Incidents: irregular spikes; they accept reactive scaling for true “unknown unknowns,” but want predictive for the known daily pattern.

Product asks (must-have)
- Autoscaling bounds:
  - Hard min baseline (protect SLA) + hard max (budget cap).
  - Clear semantics/precedence over platform defaults.
- Predictive mode:
  - Should bias scale-up ahead of ramp, but reactive saturation/queue signals must override if prediction is wrong.
  - Must not oscillate; wants cooldowns + dampening + clear reasons in logs.
- Observability:
  - Dashboard showing desired vs bounded replicas, bound-hit events, prediction vs actual, queue depth.
  - Audit trail for policy edits + scaling decisions.

Security/compliance notes
- SSO/SAML required for Console access.
- Audit logging: explicit request for “who changed min/max,” plus autoscaler decisions (“what did it want, what did bounds clamp to, and why”).
- Retention controls: asks for 12 months+ logs for compliance reviews; may settle for premium retention add-on.
- KMS: customer-managed keys for any stored config/audit logs in Private/VPC control plane.
- Data residency: flagged possible EU sub-tenant; not a blocker yet but needs an answer before expansion.

Support / escalations
- SUP-28437: queueing during daily ramp; customer asked for predictive scaling specifically.
- SUP-28479 (pilot): oscillation/jitter when predictive was enabled during a surprise spike; mitigated by disabling predictive temporarily + moving to reactive while fix landed.

Open questions (internal)
- Confirm whether they need Private control plane vs Dedicated-in-VPC only.
- Clarify audit log export path (SIEM) and whether Kevin Osei’s standard export meets their format requirements.

- Miguel Santos: set up weekly pilot cadence + capture before/after ramp metrics.
- Rachel Kim: coordinate commercial language with legal: “hard max bound enforced by platform,” baseline min, and audit log retention.
